title: U.S. Southwest semiconductor workforce and supplier scaling evidence
question: Can local supplier and workforce systems support semiconductor scaling?
why_it_matters: Funded semiconductor projects only become operating capacity if labor pipelines, construction capacity, suppliers, training systems, and capital commitments can keep up.
current_support: FTFN has national CHIPS context, MAG regional projections, a named TSMC registered technician apprenticeship with an initial eight-person cohort and a later 46-person cohort, and a City-relayed July 2026 update saying the first Arizona fab is in volume production, second-fab construction is complete, and TSMC Arizona employs more than 3,500 people.
missing_evidence: apprenticeship completion, credential, retention, and placement outcomes
training capacity relative to fab and supplier demand
facility occupation mix, vacancies, attrition, and hiring demand
candidate_records: MAG 2023 population, housing, and employment projections
TSMC apprenticeship outcome and retention data
Arizona occupation-specific labor and vacancy data
next_action: Add apprenticeship completion and retention results, occupation-level labor and hiring data, construction-trade capacity, and supplier operating records before making workforce or supplier sufficiency claims.
notes: Phase 51C replaces the pure recruitment-target view with active-cohort counts and adds a current total-employment and fab-status claim. The gap remains unresolved because neither record reports apprenticeship outcomes, occupational sufficiency, construction capacity, or supplier-network maturity.
